scope: Isolated fixed-j=1 full-gate collisions after the frozen bounded-cluster o(M) theorem
proved: For every actual j=1 prime, p divides the normalized Smith generator g_M=gcd(Cbar0(M),Cbar1(M)) if and only if p^2 divides both raw coefficients, equivalently the full gate collides.
The ideal (Cbar0,Cbar1)=g_M Z is the specialized zeroth Fitting ideal and first Smith ideal; its positive generator is the canonical integral scalar but is exactly the target gcd problem.
The full collision radical is gcd(rad(abs(g_M)),B_M^(1)) when the specialized pair is nonzero.
For any fixed isolation diameter D, the full and D-isolated collision radicals differ by only O_D(M/log M)=o(M) log weight, by frozen Item279.

On the generic rank-two graph chart, the collision ideal is two independent linear forms, has height two, and contracts to zero in the parameter field; a state-free resultant of only those two forms is identically zero.
The rank-one collision ideal is principal and the rank-zero ideal is zero; neither rank-drop stratum is discarded or given an unproved density bound.
Over each odd finite field, degree two is the smallest possible fiberwise exact scalar degree: linear forms have nonzero kernels, while X^2-dY^2 is anisotropic for nonsquare d.
The fixed norms d=-1,2,3,5,7 each have an exact actual noncollision row on which the norm of the two normalized gate values vanishes.

For every finite library of fixed nonzero integral homogeneous binary forms, Chebotarev gives infinitely many actual phase primes at which every form has a nonzero projective zero; no such library is fiberwise exact on all rows.
Every prime p>=13 embeds in the actual tied family using s=1 for p=1 mod 4 and s=2 for p=3 mod 4.
The forced Cartier product has log constant kappa=-4 log 2+pi/sqrt(3)+3 log 3=2.33704750799876..., so the inherited normalized component constant is H-kappa=3.99058003744209....
A bounded-degree scalar of maximum degree d and minimum degree e has inherited collision-radical ratio at least (d/e)(H-kappa)>=H-kappa, much worse than the raw 1/6 support.
The raw-coordinate H/2 bound from Item264 remains better than the normalized scalar route, but also exceeds 1/6.
At the normalized inherited height, at least 24 genuinely independent valuation copies would be needed merely to beat the raw j=1 support; none is proved.
Item149 de-overlap leaves the fixed-j=1 ceiling unchanged at 1/36 per 6M.
